newsitem.title: USA: GM Q1 European automotive net falls sharply.
newsitem.headline: GM Q1 European automotive net falls sharply.

text.p: General Motors Corp said operating income from its European automotive operations during the first quarter of 1997 fell to $94 million from $285 million in the year-earlier period.

GM-Europe's operating income for the first quarter excludes a $55 million after-tax gain related to the settlement of the automaker's industrial espionage dispute with Germany's Volkswagen AG in January.

"The lower earnings in the first quarter of 1997 were primarily due to reduced volumes and higher sales incentives across Europe under intensely competitive market conditions, coupled with lower equity earnings, primarily from Saab as they await the release of their new 9-5 models," GM Chairman Jack Smith said in a statement.
Saab Automobile AB is 50 percent owned by GM and 50 percent by Sweden's AB Investor.
European retail incentives rose to $622 per vehicle during the first quarter from $443 a year earlier.
Including the gain from the VW settlement, the European results brought first quarter net income for GM's International Operations to $317 million, down from $432 million a year earlier.
The remainder of GM's International Operations, including Latin American and Asia and Pacific Operations, earned first quarter net income of $168 million, up from $147 million in the year-ago period.
GM said its international wholesale vehicle sales to dealers in the first quarter totaled 783,000 units versus 792,000 a year earlier.
